title: They thought they were rich.
paragraphs:
You can sit in worship…
and still be spiritually numb.

You can say “God is good”…
while your heart is far from Him.

You can look alive in public…
and be dying in private.
And if we’re honest… that’s some of us.
Because the scariest kind of lost is not rebellion.

No fire.
No hunger.
No trembling before God.

You sing—but don’t surrender.
You pray—but don’t repent.
You serve—but don’t love Jesus.
You stop feeling your need for Him.
“Because you say, ‘I am rich, have become wealthy, and have need of nothing’—and do not know that you are wretched, miserable, poor, blind, and naked.” (Revelation 3:17, NKJV)
This is pride at its most dangerous form.
And pride like that will blind you faster than sin you openly fight.
Because at least the broken know they’re broken.
They feel whole… while rotting inside.
Some scholars interpret Laodicea’s wealth as both material and spiritual complacency—meaning they had external success, but internal decay.
You can be blessed… and still be blind.
Respected… and still be far from Christ.
And here’s where the story cuts deep—
“Behold, I stand at the door and knock…” (Revelation 3:20, NKJV)
And maybe that’s you right now.
With a version of Christianity that requires nothing from you.
Jesus doesn’t expose you to shame you.
He exposes you to save you.
“As many as I love, I rebuke and chasten. Therefore be zealous and repent.” (Revelation 3:19, NKJV)
Because real love will not let you stay blind.
Real love will confront your pride.
Real love will call you back.
You are more sinful than you admit.
But you are more loved than you can imagine.

You are blind…
but Jesus gives sight.

You are poor…
but Jesus became poor so you could become rich in Him.

You are naked…
but Jesus was stripped on the cross to clothe you in righteousness.
“For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though He was rich, yet for your sakes He became poor, that you through His poverty might become rich.” (2 Corinthians 8:9, NKJV)
Jesus didn’t die for perfect people.
So that anyone who repents and believes in Him will be forgiven, restored, and made new.
Is Jesus inside… or still knocking?
Come back to the One you replaced.
He sits with those who once shut Him out.
“To him who overcomes I will grant to sit with Me on My throne…” (Revelation 3:21, NKJV)
Where are you really with Him?
If something in you is stirring… that’s not emotion.
